changes: AWS growth is now guided, not hoped for: 39.3% in 3Q ($46.0bn, $184bn run rate) and Jassy projects over 40% in both 2027 and 2028, with backlog up to $578bn (+16.5% QoQ, +189% YoY) and margin 38.7% with only $91mn of energy-derivative help.

The build stopped being self-funded: 3Q cash capex $75.9bn (+43% QoQ, 1.8x operating cash flow), quarterly FCF -$33.5bn and TTM FCF -$42.4bn; 2027 capex 'meaningfully more' than about $220bn, with no number.

Amazon now borrows like a builder: face debt $180.9bn (+$47.9bn QoQ; $68.8bn at year-end), the $17.5bn term loan drawn at SOFR+62.5-87.5bp, and a new secured supplier loan facility of up to about $80bn (Q1 2027 to Q3 2028), its first debt secured on purchased equipment.
Off-balance-sheet commitments jumped: leases not yet commenced $164.9bn (+$27.7bn QoQ), total commitments $883.6bn (+36%), energy contracts 690mn MWh (from 270mn) over about 18 years.
Jassy put a number on the neocloud penalty: neocloud capacity is 'about 3,500 basis points worse in operating margin' than long-leased capacity, and most AWS capacity is owned or long-leased.

consensus_thesis: Investors own Amazon as the AI capacity landlord whose AWS growth re-accelerated on a $496bn backlog anchored by Anthropic and OpenAI, and pay about 23.5x FY27 EPS for mid-to-high-30s AWS growth and 2027 capex that earns its keep.
headline: Consensus should raise AWS growth and keep the landlord thesis, but drop any assumption that the build pays for itself: Amazon's AI compounding improves while its credit quality weakens at the margin, as debt, secured equipment loans and $165bn of uncommenced leases fund the gap.
kona: Amazon's CEO said neocloud capacity carries about 3,500bp lower operating margin than long-leased capacity, so the product Amazon wants from Kona is a long lease on a powered shell, not GPU-as-a-service. Its blocks are 'hundreds of megawatts or sometimes up to a gigawatt', so at tens of MW Kona should target labs, inference tenants or a developer aggregating for a hyperscaler, and copy the Cipher-style parent-guaranteed lease. Owning GPUs means competing against an AA buyer that can now finance chips through a variable-rate secured vendor facility of up to about $80bn; Kona should not bet its equity on that spread.
monitor: 4Q cash capex: the unchanged ~$220bn FY26 guide implies only ~$47.8bn in 4Q (vs $75.9bn in 3Q); a 2027 number when given in February.
Funding mix: first draws and terms on the ~$80bn secured supplier facility, 2027 bond plans, and any rating outlook change from A1/AA/AA-.
Backlog breadth: any concentration disclosure for the $578bn (Anthropic, OpenAI) and whether 4Q AWS growth reaches 40%.

sections.body: More: Multi-year AWS growth targets (>40% in 2027 and 2028); 'trillion dollar' AWS in 5-10 years; Bedrock and inference (tokens ~17x); Trainium external sales from late 2027; owned/long-leased capacity vs neoclouds; useful-life extension and faster break-even. Less or dropped: Power capacity 'doubling by end-2027' (2Q call) not repeated in the sources read; no GW added; no quantified 2027 capex; no free cash flow, debt or lease commentary on the call. KPIs more important: Quarterly FCF and capex/OCF; face debt and secured borrowing; leases not yet commenced; backlog weighted life (6.4 to 6.1 yrs); AWS D&A as % of AWS revenue (20.1%). KPIs less important: Energy-derivative adjustment to AWS margin (only $91mn in 3Q); retail margin noise from Prime Day timing. Risks up: Funding and leverage; off-balance-sheet commitments; capex inflation from memory and components; lab exposure through stakes. Risks down: AWS deceleration and backlog conversion; AWS margin compression (held at 38.7%).

head: Question
Why it matters / asked?
rows: The 10-Q discloses a secured supplier loan facility of up to about $80bn from Q1 2027. What assets secure it, what is the pricing, and will secured debt be capped as a share of total debt to protect unsecured noteholders?
Quarterly FCF was -$33.5bn and face debt rose $47.9bn in a quarter. What is the 2027 range for net debt issuance, and at what lease-adjusted leverage would you slow capex?
Credit. Asked in part (Anmuth); deflected ('We can fund this plan').
Leases not yet commenced rose $27.7bn to $164.9bn. How many MW does that cover, and what share is with third-party developers under parent guarantees like Cipher's Stingray?
You call the backlog 'well-diversified'. What share of the $578bn is Anthropic and OpenAI, and why did weighted life fall to 6.1 years from 6.4?
The ~$220bn FY26 guide implies 4Q capex of about $47.8bn after $75.9bn in 3Q. Was 3Q pulled forward by component prepurchases, or will FY26 exceed $220bn?
You said neoclouds are about 3,500bp worse in operating margin. How much third-party capacity do you rent today, and will you let those contracts roll off as owned capacity lands?
Equity; read-across to neocloud credit. Answered in part (Sandler).
